title: Jest Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Jest lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Your first Jest test
entries.summary: Jest runs a test function and reports whether its checks pass. expect gives the actual value; a matcher states the expected result.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("adds two prices", () => { expect(2 + 3).toBe(5); });

notes: Save test code in a test file matched by your local Jest setup.

entries.name: Compare object contents
entries.summary: toEqual checks values inside objects. This is different from checking whether two names refer to the exact same object.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("book fields", () => { expect({ title: "Moon" }).toEqual({ title: "Moon" }); });

notes: Use toBe for object identity only when identity is the behaviour you need.

entries.name: Check lists and text
entries.summary: A length check and a containment check answer different questions about a list.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reading list", () => { const books = ["Moon", "Ocean"]; expect(books).toHaveLength(2); expect(books).toContain("Moon"); });

notes: Having the right length does not prove the right values are present.

entries.name: Check an error
entries.summary: Pass a function to toThrow so Jest can call it and catch the error.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("rejects bad age", () => { const reject = () => { throw new Error("Bad age"); }; expect(reject).toThrow("Bad age"); });

notes: Do not call the throwing function before passing it to expect.

entries.name: Set up fresh state
entries.summary: beforeEach runs before each test in its scope. Use it to prepare fresh mutable data.
notes: Do not rely on another test to clean up your state.

entries.name: Use a mock function
entries.summary: jest.fn makes a function that records calls. A mock can stand in for a small dependency.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("saves a score", () => { const save = jest.fn(); save(8); expect(save).toHaveBeenCalledWith(8); });

notes: A mock records calls; it does not prove a real database connection works.

entries.name: Choose a mock return value
entries.summary: A mock can return a chosen value so the code under test has predictable input.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reads a name", () => { const getName = jest.fn().mockReturnValue("Asha"); expect(getName()).toBe("Asha"); });

notes: Keep the fake behaviour consistent with the real dependency's contract.

entries.name: Wait for a promise
entries.summary: An async test can await a promise. resolves checks the value with which it finishes successfully.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("loads a score", async () => { await expect(Promise.resolve(8)).resolves.toBe(8); });

notes: Forgetting await or return can let an async test finish too early.

entries.name: Check promise rejection
entries.summary: rejects checks a promise that fails. It is useful for an expected error path.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reports missing data", async () => { await expect(Promise.reject(new Error("Missing"))).rejects.toThrow("Missing"); });

notes: An expected rejected promise is different from an unhandled error.

entries.name: Run a table of cases
entries.summary: test.each runs a test with each row of data. A row contains inputs and expected output.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test.each([[2, 4], [3, 6], [0, 0]])("double %i is %i", (input, expected) => { expect(input * 2).toBe(expected); });

notes: Keep table rows small enough to understand without a second program.

entries.name: Control a timer
entries.summary: Fake timers let a test move time forward without really waiting. Restore real timers when the test ends.

example.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reminder runs later", () => { jest.useFakeTimers(); try { const remind = jest.fn(); setTimeout(remind, 1000); jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000); expect(remind).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); } finally { jest.useRealTimers(); } });

notes: Leaving fake timers active can affect later tests.

entries.name: Review snapshots thoughtfully
entries.summary: A snapshot stores an expected structure. Review changes instead of accepting a new snapshot blindly.
notes: Updating every snapshot without reading it can approve a mistake.
